learningObjective: Enumerate the dependence conditions under which a loop can be parallelized across iterations.
stem: Which of the following are TRUE preconditions for a compiler to legally parallelize a loop's iterations (e.g., `#pragma omp parallel for`, or emit them as independent CUDA threads/blocks)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: No two distinct iterations write to the same memory location (no output dependence).
No iteration reads a location that a different iteration writes (no true / anti dependence across iterations).

For a reduction (e.g., `s += a[i]`), the reduction operator is treated as associative/commutative so that partial results can be combined in any order, or the language exposes an explicit `reduction(...)` clause.
The loop body must be entirely branch-free; any conditional inside the loop makes parallelization illegal.
The loop must have a compile-time-known trip count; parallelization of a loop with a runtime-known trip count is illegal.

explanation: Parallelization requires the absence of cross-iteration dependences on the same memory location. A (output dependence: WAW), B (true/anti dependence: RAW/WAR across iterations), and C (reduction treated with an appropriate associative combiner) are the standard legality conditions. Branch-free bodies (D) and compile-time trip counts (E) are neither required — SIMT / OpenMP happily parallelize branchy bodies (with warp divergence penalties) and runtime trip counts (`omp parallel for` on a variable N is standard).

optionExplanations.B: Correct: RAW/WAR across iterations blocks parallelization without reordering.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: reductions require an associative combiner or an explicit clause.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: branchy bodies are legal to parallelize; divergence is a performance concern, not legality.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: runtime trip counts are routinely parallelized.

assumptions: Statements have no external I/O or non-reentrant side effects.
Reductions, when present, use an associative combiner or an explicit reduction clause.
nonImplications: Does not imply parallelization is beneficial; small trip counts or memory-bound bodies may under-utilize parallel hardware.
Does not imply FP-associativity concerns are ignored in every context; numerical libraries may require deterministic ordering.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses warp-divergence performance concerns with legality.
distractorRationales.E: Confuses trip-count knowability with parallelization legality.
